must_remember: The de Broglie wavelength associated with a particle of mass $m$ and velocity $v$ is given by $\lambda = \frac{h}{mv}$.
For an electron accelerated through a potential $V$, the de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}} \text{ \AA}$.
The Davisson-Germer experiment confirmed the wave nature of electrons using nickel single crystal diffraction at $54\text{ V}$ and $50^{\circ}$.
The group velocity ($v_g$) of matter waves equals the classical particle velocity $v$, whereas the phase velocity ($v_p$) exceeds the speed of light ($c^2/v$).
Heisenberg's position-momentum uncertainty principle is expressed as $\Delta x \cdot \Delta p \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}$.

glossary.meaning: The wavelength associated with a moving material particle, inversely proportional to its momentum.
The velocity with which a phase of a wave propagates; for matter waves, $v_p = \frac{c^2}{v} > c$.
The velocity of the wave packet representing a moving particle, equal to the particle's classical velocity $v$.
An intrinsic fundamental limit to the simultaneous precision of conjugate dynamical variables.
